item.title: Live Updates: Trial begins for Lindsay Clancy in murders of her 3 kids
item.description: Lindsay Clancy, accused of killing her three young children in her Duxbury, Massachusetts, home in 2023, is standing trial. Follow along with live updates during opening statements and testimony on Monday.

item.title: U.S.-Iran war appears to pause as Trump gives "diplomacy a chance"
item.description: The U.S. and Iran hold fire amid work on a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, but the Trump administration says a military buildup continues.

item.title: Cracker Barrel CEO who oversaw controversial logo redesign to step down
item.description: Masino will be replaced on Aug. 10 by David Deno, most recently the CEO of Bloomin' Brands.

item.title: Two strangers separated by generations met on a train ride. The encounter changed their lives
item.description: A train ride encounter between two strangers separated by generations led to weekly dinners and a trip to Puerto Rico. CBS News contributor David Begnaud explains how the two lives are now forever connected.

item.title: Paul de Gelder talks about dangerous mission to track the largest great white shark
item.description: Shark attack survivor and advocate Paul de Gelder talks to "CBS Mornings" about his high-risk mission to search for one of the largest sharks in the North Atlantic as part of this year's "Shark Week" on the Discovery Channel. He also addresses how he overcame his fear of sharks.

item.title: Keep your health goals on track throughout the summer
item.description: Between vacations and barbecues, summer can throw off your fitness routine. Celebrity trainer Kira Stokes has tips on how to stay consistent all summer long.

item.title: U.S.-Iran fighting paused as progress reported in talks to reopen Strait of Hormuz
item.description: After two weeks of strikes and despite threats from President Trump to escalate the war in Iran by hitting civilian targets, there's a pause in fighting between the two countries. It comes amid progress in talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, sources in Iran and Oman say. Charlie D'Agata reports.

item.title: Oil prices tumble, stock set to rise amid pause in U.S.-Iran fighting
item.description: Stock futures rose and crude fell after U.S. Ambassador Mike Waltz told "Face the Nation" that a pause in U.S.-Iran fighting aims to give diplomacy time to work.

item.title: U.S. mom and kids trapped by French wildfire: "Such an unstable situation"
item.description: A mother from Tennessee slept through wildfire evacuation operations in southwest France, and now she's trapped with her kids as the blaze threatens the city Bordeaux.

item.title: Should Democrats be concerned about Graham Platner's replacement in Maine?
item.description: Democrat Troy Jackson is set to replace Graham Platner in the Maine Senate race. CBS News contributor Chuck Rocha and managing principal at The Vogel Group, Samir Kapadia, have more.

item.title: Woman charged with murdering her 3 children goes on trial
item.description: A Massachusetts woman goes on trial Monday, charged with murdering her three children. Lindsay Clancy has pleaded not guilty. Her attorneys say she had severe postpartum mental health issues and her doctor's treatment only made them worse. CBS News legal analyst Caroline Polisi has more on the case.

item.title: 6 things debt collectors don't want you to know about
item.description: Before you answer another collection call or decide on a solution, make sure you know these important facts.

item.title: 1.6 million cartons of eggs are recalled over potential salmonella contamination
item.description: The recall affects white-shell and cage-free eggs sold under multiple grocery brands in six states. No illnesses have been reported.

item.title: GOP targeted progressive dark money. That could boomerang on Trump.
item.description: The Trump-linked group Freedom 250 staged America's birthday with tens of millions that it is not required to disclose.

item.title: Where will silver and gold prices head this August? Experts weigh in
item.description: Could gold and silver prices rebound this August after declining in recent months? Here's what some experts think.

item.title: ICE plans to target Haitians as their Temporary Protected Status ends, sources say
item.description: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement plans to ramp up deportations of Haitians as their Temporary Protected Status expires, sources say. CBS News' Camilo Montoya-Galvez has more.

item.title: Berlin Pride attacker served time for trying to join ISIS, officials say
item.description: The suspect, identified as 21-year-old Abdul Ballout, was killed in a confrontation with police in a suburb of Berlin, police said.

item.title: Behind LeBron James' move to the 76ers and his chances for another NBA title
item.description: NBA veteran Wally Szczerbiak, who's an analyst for CBS Sports and MSG Networks, talks with "CBS Mornings" about LeBron James' decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers and if he can win another NBA title.

item.title: What's happening with the Strait of Hormuz as U.S. halts Iran strikes after apparent talks progress
item.description: The U.S. paused its strikes on Iran after 13 days, while apparent progress is being made toward a deal between Oman and Iran, an official told CBS News. Courtney Kealy has more.

item.title: Berlin Pride attack suspect served prison time for trying to join ISIS, German prosecutors say
item.description: The 21-year-old suspect who killed one person and injured at least 29 others after ramming a car into a crowd during a Berlin Pride event served prison time for trying to join ISIS, German prosecutors say. CBS News' Anna Noryskiewicz has the latest.

item.title: What's known about the North Carolina mom who went missing in Grenada
item.description: Authorities are searching for a mom from North Carolina who disappeared during a Caribbean vacation. Elizabeth Waddell was last seen Wednesday on the beach in Grenada's capital city. She didn't return to the home she was sharing with a friend. Cristian Benavides reports.

item.title: Trump takes swings at journalists at White House Correspondents' Dinner
item.description: President Trump took swings at journalists during his remarks at the rescheduled White House Correspondents' Dinner, calling them "the largest group of Trump derangement syndrome people." Eli Lake, host of The Free Press podcast "Breaking History," joins with more. Paramount Skydance owns The Free Press and CBS News.

item.title: Americans are eating less produce amid cyclospora outbreak, CBS News poll finds
item.description: Amid the outbreak of cyclospora, a CBS News poll finds 40% of Americans say they are buying or eating less produce. Nearly half of those polled say they have little or no confidence in the FDA to deal with the outbreak. Carter Evans reports.

item.title: Remains found by kayakers identified as woman missing since 1985
item.description: Human remains found in a Florida canal two years ago have been identified as those of a woman who vanished in 1985, police said.

item.title: What's known about the suspect in the Berlin LGBTQ+ parade attack
item.description: Police in Germany say they shot and killed the suspect who drove a van into a crowd at an LGBTQ+ parade on Saturday, killing one person and injuring dozens. The suspect was known to have extreme views. Chris Livesay reports.

item.title: Video appears to show person kicking sea lion: "Disgusting act"
item.description: The video appears to show a person throwing kicks at the sea lion at La Jolla Cove as at least one other person can be heard laughing in the background.

item.title: Cyclospora boosts fears that deadlier foodborne outbreaks are ahead
item.description: Food safety experts say cuts to the public health system hobbled the response — and that the next outbreak could be much worse.

item.title: Emotional ceremony for 3 inducted into Baseball Hall of Fame
item.description: Center fielders Carlos Beltrán and Andruw Jones and second baseman Jeff Kent were inducted into the Baseball Hall of Fame on Sunday.

item.title: More than 300,000 displaced in France and Spain as wildfires rage
item.description: Forests in Spain and France have been parched by successive heatwaves since May that have brought drought to many areas.

item.title: ICE to target Haitians as Temporary Protected Status is set to end, sources say
item.description: The plans include arresting migrants in Ohio and quickly putting them on deportation flights to crisis-stricken Haiti, the internal documents indicate.
